result.title: Shoot for the moon — so we can help the Earth #TEDTalks
result.description: Philosopher Meghan Sullivan and space architect Ariel Ekblaw don't usually work at the same altitude ... but put them in a room together, and they'll answer the big questions. Drawing on wisdom from Aristotle to astronauts, they discuss what humans inherently owe each other, what it takes to live a good life and what a rulebook for a better world might look like.

result.title: Who Controls Your City’s Money? | Trinity Tran | TED
result.description:
What if your city could borrow money from its own bank instead of private lenders? TED Fellow Trinity Tran is leading the push for public banks — which are owned by the people through their local governments — and shows how this model could ensure your local tax dollars stay in your community.  (Recorded at TED Fellows Films 2026 on April 14, 2026)

result.title: How AI Is Breaking the Internet (and What to Do About It) | Matthew Prince | TED
result.description:
For the past 30 years, surviving as an internet business meant getting people to click on your website. But AI is now making that thousands of times harder, says Matthew Prince, CEO of Cloudflare, one of the world’s largest internet networks. He makes the provocative case for a different deal — whereby tech companies actually pay people for creating content that feeds their AI models. (Recorded at TED2026 on April 16, 2026)

result.title: The key to a K-pop hit? Vocal fry and fruit innuendos #TEDTalks
result.description: Want to become a K-pop superstar? Comedian and musician Charlene Kaye lays out the formula for breaking through in just a few easy steps, from rapping like a sexy baby to dancing like you’re making pizza in the Matrix. Part musical, part dance performance, part comedy show — this is your how-to guide for creating the next K-pop hit.
